Mrs. Fisher: I saw the catfish you caught. Nice piece, kid.
You: Thanks.
Mrs. Fisher: That reminds me, remember when we talked about catching fish with bare hands?
You: Yes? What about it? 
Mrs. Fisher: In the southern states, mostly Alabama and Oklahoma, there are people called noodlers.
You: Noodlers?
Mrs. Fisher: It’s a group of people that catches catfish with their bare hands.
You: How is that even possible?
Mrs. Fisher: They go underwater, looking for a hole at the bottom in which the catfish protects its eggs. When they find it, they provoke the fish to bite their foot or hand and then drag it out of the water.
Mrs. Fisher: It’s very dangerous, these fishes sometimes weigh over 100 pounds and can knock out a noodler with their powerful bodies. That’s why a spotter is a must when noodling, especially in deep water.
You: It was quite a fight to get it. I can’t even imagine what it’s like to catch one that big with bare hands.
Mrs. Fisher: If you ever try it, better wear gloves. The fish won’t bite your hand off, but it will leave a nasty bruise.
You: Yeah, I doubt I will ever try it.
Mrs. Fisher: A shame. It’s actually a lot of fun. I had to stop noodling after a certain wardrobe malfunction incident.
You: That’s…{{wi}} I’m sorry to hear that.
Mrs. Fisher: Don’t worry. In the end, they dropped the charges and I didn’t end up in the sex offender's registry.
You: …
